title: What a kingdom council does, and what the game now does for it
body_md:
**Two layers of power.** The game defines the **king** and the titles and skills that come with the throne, and below the king the **alliance ranks** (leader, Counselors, officers with customisable permissions) [B03-0003, B04-0001]. Everything else (the council, DKP, MGE lists, intake and exit rules) is made by the community and **varies by kingdom** [B03-0004, B03-0005].

**What a council does, in ten recurring jobs** (this guide's summary of the practice cards below, not a measured list): agree the rules before KvK; pick who enters the Lost Kingdom; set and score requirements (DKP); manage exits; screen migrants; allocate MGE; hand out titles; keep alliances tidy; run event sign-ups; and handle diplomacy.

**Since 2025 official tools cover part of this work:**

| Job | Official tool (patch) | Still done outside the game |
|---|---|---|
| Titles | Title reservation with king/ruler approval or auto-approval (1.0.91), CH requirement per title (1.0.94) [B03-0002] | Little; some kingdoms still run queues or title bots |
| Who enters the Lost Kingdom | Domains (1.0.91, 600-governor rule 1.1.01) and battle roster for single-domain kingdoms (1.1.00), roster import code from the ROK Toolkit (1.1.02) [B02-0001]; Watchlist king skill (1.1.00) [B02-0002] | Publishing the selection criteria |
| Alliance housekeeping | 6 officer permission categories (1.0.96) [B04-0001]; Alliance Notes and Quick Checks (1.1.07) [B04-0002] | Private officer records, activity history |
| Combat coordination | Army Groups and map markers (pioneer 1.1.01; Army Groups for all SoC alliances 1.1.02) [B04-0005] | Cross-timezone scheduling |
| SoC diplomacy | Team-ups (1.0.95), match vote and coalitions (1.1.03), Rest Mode vote (1.1.08, pioneer) [B09-0002] | Agreements inside the kingdom |
| DKP and requirements | **None found.** Our review found no official per-governor stats export in notes 1.0.90–1.1.09 [B08-0003, organizado]; DKP has no official definition [B08-0001]. The ROK Toolkit's contents are unknown [B08-0007] | Scans, formula, publishing |
| Intake | Partial: a T3 guide says the king sets the normal immigration power cap and approves special immigration; official notes confirm only that special immigration exists (1.1.03) [B06-0002] | Screening applicants |
| MGE allocation, exit lists | **None found** in the cards | All of it |

**Default for a new council:** use every official tool for the jobs it covers, and spend your written rules and volunteer time on the jobs it does not (DKP, MGE, intake screening, exits).
why_md: Councils lose time maintaining bots, sheets and chat queues for jobs the game already does (titles are the clearest case [B03-0002]), while the jobs that cause the worst disputes (DKP, MGE, exits) have no official support at all. Knowing the split tells you where written rules and trusted people are needed.
uncertain_notes: B03-0004 (one leadership team / council per kingdom) is organizado/baixa: a community norm from a few voices. B03-0005 (informal enforcement) and B08-0003 (no official export found) are organizado. B06-0002 (king's immigration cap and approval) is organizado/media; the king's control of the cap is T3 only. The list of ten jobs is this guide's synthesis. Everything else in the table is official patch notes (verificado/alta).

title: Roles and official powers: king, Queen/General/PM, R5, officers
body_md:
| Role | Official powers | Card |
|---|---|---|
| **King** | Chooses which titles are open to reservation, auto-approval and durations (1.0.91; CH requirement per title 1.0.94); **Watchlist** king skill (1.1.00); battle roster in single-domain kingdoms (1.1.00) and activating extra domains at Lost Kingdom registration; Vacation Permits once the kingdom is in SoC (1.0.87); Rest Mode vote (1.1.08, pioneer); *reported by a T3 guide only:* sets the normal immigration power cap and approves special immigration | B03-0002, B02-0002, B02-0001, B03-0007, C04-0031, B06-0002 |
| **Queen, General, Prime Minister** | Since 1.0.96, in kingdoms and Lost Kingdom domains, can use **Imprison, Exile, Banish, Leader and Inspire** (these five skills only) | B03-0003 |
| **"Rulers"** | The notes say kings and rulers can approve title reservations (1.0.91) and that rulers can manage the Watchlist (1.1.03); kings and rulers cannot be targeted by Watchlist or Banish (1.1.03). **Who counts as a ruler is not defined in the notes** (gap L-B03-04); do not assume it means Queen/General/PM until checked in game | B02-0002, B03-0002 |
| **Alliance leader (R5) and Counselors** | Customise each officer title's permissions across 6 categories (1.0.96); can cancel a building dismantle (1.1.03) | B04-0001 |
| **Officers** | Whatever their title is granted; with permission: Alliance Notes and Quick Checks (1.1.07), coalition markers; officers place map alliance and teleport markers (1.1.01) | B04-0001, B04-0002, B04-0005 |

**Watchlist limits (1.1.01):** it cannot target the top 100 by individual power in Imperium kingdoms or the top 50 in other kingdoms, but anyone under 50M power can be watchlisted regardless of rank; watchlisting someone already in the Lost Kingdom sends them home [B02-0002].

**Banish** (king skill since 1.0.74) teleports a city to a random spot in the kingdom's upper-left province [B03-0003].

**Do this (advice):** a T3 guide says the king assigns Queen, General and Prime Minister [B03-0001]; give those titles to trusted council members in **different time zones**, so the five shared skills (Imprison, Exile, Banish, Leader, Inspire) are available around the clock. The other king powers above are not shared with them by any note we found.
why_md: Since 1.0.96 five king skills can be shared with the Queen, General and Prime Minister [B03-0003]. A kingdom where only the king can act stops working while the king sleeps or quits. The Watchlist's top-50/100 protection means it cannot be used against the strongest accounts unless they are under 50M power [B02-0002], so plan rules that do not depend on it for them.
uncertain_notes: B06-0002 is organizado/media: the king's control of the normal immigration cap and approval of special immigration come from a T3 guide; official notes only confirm that special immigration exists (1.1.03). B03-0001 (the king assigns Queen/General/PM) is organizado/media, T3 guides. C04-0031 (Rest Mode vote, pioneer) is a patch-state card. Who "rulers" are is undefined (L-B03-04). Effects and cooldowns of Imprison, Exile, Leader and Inspire were not collected.

title: Write the kingdom rules down before KvK1, and publish them where players see them
body_md:
**What to write down (one page per item is enough):**
1. **Who leads:** the council members, the king, who holds Queen/General/PM, and how the council decides.
2. **Territory and flags:** which alliance holds which zone.
3. **DKP formula and requirement**, with the date they apply from (see the DKP block).
4. **MGE policy:** model, who gets the top slots, point caps for everyone else, penalty for breaking it.
5. **Intake:** migration requirements, application route, which alliance new arrivals join.
6. **Exits and enforcement:** what triggers a removal, notice period, appeal.
7. **Titles:** which are reservable and on what terms.
8. **Conduct:** no scripts or cheats (Conduct Score) and no sharing of logins.

**Where kingdoms publish (practice):** some kingdoms keep rule sites with pages for immigration, rules, DKP, titles and Ark of Osiris; many rely on unwritten rules passed on in chat or Discord [B07-0002]. Discord is the usual hub [B07-0001], and leaders are reported to broadcast through in-game mail and chat [B07-0003].

**Official in-game places:** the **Kingdom Bugle** and **Lost Kingdom Bugle** pin a statement to the top of kingdom/Lost Kingdom chat (1.0.91); mail; alliance and coalition voice chat (1.0.99) [B07-0004]. No in-game translation feature appears in the 1.0.90–1.1.09 notes [B07-0004], so multilingual kingdoms need translated copies.

**Our default:** keep one written source (site or document), pin a short summary with a link in the Bugle, and mail every change with its date.
why_md: Unwritten rules are the main way newcomers get punished for things nobody told them: one first-KvK player received a requirement of 250% of power by mail without knowing what DKP meant [B08-0002]. In some kingdoms migrants are expected to ask the king before moving, and one player reported that nothing in the game warned them of that rule [B03-0006]. A written, dated rule also gives the council something to point to in a dispute instead of a memory of a chat message.
uncertain_notes: B07-0002 (rule sites vs unwritten rules; only 2 sites found, sharing a template), B07-0003 (mail and chat as broadcast channels) and B03-0006 (approval-before-migrating norm) are organizado/baixa. B07-0001 and B08-0002 are organizado/media. The list of what to write down is this guide's synthesis of the jobs in the overview block, not a measured practice.

title: DKP and requirements: design principles (the weights are your kingdom's choice)
body_md:
**DKP is not a game feature.** Each kingdom sets its own weights, usually ignoring T1–T3 kills and weighting deaths most [B08-0001]. **This guide does not recommend weights**; they are a kingdom decision. The verified examples show how far they differ:

| Source | Formula, quoted from the source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| K2708 kingdom site (KvK1) | "DKP = T4 kill * 10 + T5 kill * 20 + death * 50." | |
| K2779 kingdom site (KvK2) | "DKP = T4 kill * 10 + T5 kill * 30 + death * 80." | "T1, T2, T3 kills are not included. If you are zeroed with terrible trade, your death of that day will be counted as 0." |
| ROK Steward (example in the tool) | "Excel formula = T4 × 1 + T5 × 2 + Deads × 10" | optional raw KP weight and group bonuses/penalties |

[B08-0001]. These are examples of what other kingdoms chose, not recommended values. The two kingdom sites share a template, so treat them as one norm with two parameter sets.

**Requirements (reported practice):** often a DKP target proportional to power (flat or power-tiered), sometimes adjusted by account age, seed or group, and measured as the **change between a start and an end scan** [B08-0002].

**Design principles the evidence supports:**
- **Publish formula and requirement before KvK**, dated, and explain what DKP means. First-KvK players receive targets without explanation [B08-0002].
- **State which power is the base** (start-scan power, troop power...). Sources do not say what kingdoms use, so you must define it.
- **Score the delta between a start and an end scan** (as the requirement sources describe) and keep an **exception log** (e.g. the K2779 rule for zeroed-day deaths) [B08-0001].
- **If your data comes from scans, join on governor ID.** In one scanner's documentation, kingdom scans capture IDs; honor/alliance/seed ranking scans give only an approximate name, so honor must be matched by name [B08-0004].
- **Say how alts are handled.** Some kingdoms combine a governor's accounts onto one for DKP [B08-0006].
- **Know the official metric.** **Acclaim** is earned from severe wounds and kills inflicted and suffered, scaled by troop level (SoC Lost Kingdoms, 1.1.01); 1.1.04 cut T1 rates to 1 Acclaim per 10,000 T1 severely wounded and 2 per 10,000 killed [C04-0015]. **Uncertain:** one commercial third-party summary, unverified, says 1.1.12 extends Acclaim to Seasons 1–2 [C04-0002].

**After KvK:** some kingdoms are reported to tier governors into reward / probation / removal [B08-0006]; see the exits block.
why_md: No standard formula exists, and in the three verified examples the death weight is 2.5× to 5× the T5-kill weight [B08-0001], so copying another kingdom's numbers copies its priorities, not a rule. The weights are your kingdom's choice. What players dispute is usually not the weights but surprise: a target they did not know, a base they did not understand, or an exception made for someone else. The principles above remove the surprise whatever weights you choose.
uncertain_notes: B08-0002 (requirements as % of power, deltas) and B08-0006 (post-KvK tiers, alts combined) are organizado (media/baixa): reported practice, not mechanics. C04-0002 (Acclaim in Seasons 1–2, 1.1.12) is a single commercial T3 source that garbles other details, bruto/baixa (C04-0015's own notes say Seasons 1–3). C04-0015 is a patch-state card (official notes, bruto). Only three formulas were verified; the 'publish/define/log' principles are this guide's reasoning.

title: Getting the numbers: check the official ROK Toolkit first; scanners carry ToS risk
body_md:
**What the game gives officially (our review of the notes):** per-governor profiles and rankings, and a personal "development overview" graph (1.0.91); **no per-governor stats export** appears in the official notes 1.0.90–1.1.09 [B08-0003].

**The ROK Toolkit.** Lilith runs an official in-game **ROK Toolkit**, reached from the Notice Board, described as having "tons of info about every Kingdom"; since 1.1.02 it turns an uploaded battle roster into a roster code [B08-0007]. What governor data it shows, who can open it and whether it exports anything is **unknown** (pending in-game check, T0). **Open it before you pay for or build anything else.**

**How kingdoms get stats today (reported practice, not a recommendation):** self-run scanners, paid scan services, free analytics, or hired scanners, then DKP in spreadsheets [B08-0003]. Self-run scanners drive the game client through an emulator with ADB [B08-0004], i.e. they are automation.

**The risk:** the Terms of Service text (version shown 2025-04-15) bars accessing or downloading game content with robots, crawlers or data-mining tools and accessing the services by automated means [C02-0003, C02-0004]. Since 1.1.07, players who use third-party tools such as scripts or cheats have their **Conduct Score** deducted, with penalties below thresholds (rolled out first in SoC kingdoms) [C04-0006]. Whether a given scanner triggers Conduct Score is not documented. This guide does not recommend scanners, scan services or any automation on the game client.

**Lower-risk habits:** take numbers from official screens and the Toolkit; keep the formula and the resulting sheet in a shared council document, not in one person's tool.
why_md: Without an official export, kingdoms report depending on scanners or paid services [B08-0003] and on whoever runs them. If the Toolkit already shows kingdom stats, much of that work and risk disappears; if it does not, the council should at least know the ToS and Conduct Score risk and avoid making the kingdom depend on one person's scanner.
uncertain_notes: B08-0003 (no official export found; scan services) is organizado/media and conflicts with C02-0016's unverified in-game export hypothesis (organizado/baixa). C02-0003 and C02-0004 (ToS clauses) are organizado/alta: literal ToS text, not yet checked against a newer ToS version. C04-0006 is a patch-state card; how Conduct Score treats scanners or scan services is not stated.

title: Lost Kingdom / KvK preparation: timeline, registration, battle roster, roles
body_md:
**Timeline (first KvK, approximate):** third-party guides (game version unknown) put pre-KvK (Eve of the Crusade) around kingdom day 85–95 and KvK1 around day 100 [B01-0500]. **Uncertain:** one commercial summary of 1.1.12, unverified and garbled in places, says Eve of the Crusade now opens together with the Lost Kingdom [C04-0002]; if so, the separate pre-KvK phase in those guides no longer applies (gap L-B01-03). Check the in-game event calendar. KvK durations per season are contested in the sources [B01-0502]; per-story day-by-day timelines are not collected.

**Registration (official):**
- Kingdoms are split into domains by activity level (1.0.91); since 1.1.01 a domain unlocks at **600+ active governors** and holds up to **600** [B02-0001].
- Single-domain kingdoms have a **battle roster**: the king selects which governors participate (1.1.00). Only one domain is active at registration by default; the king can activate more up to the cap; **domains lock when registration ends** [B02-0001].
- Since 1.1.02 you can **upload the roster in the ROK Toolkit**, get a roster code, and paste it in the Lost Kingdom Domain interface [B02-0001, B08-0007].
- **Watchlist** (king skill, 1.1.00) keeps a governor out of the Lost Kingdom (limits in the roles block) [B02-0002].
- **Quick Checks** (1.1.07, alliance-wide confirm/decline) unlock when the kingdom enters Season 1 [B04-0002].

**Schedule of passes and ruins:** leaders build or look for per-story spreadsheets (practice, evidence 2023–2025); Lilith said in Apr 2025 it was working on an in-KvK calendar, but no patch note through 1.1.09 announces it. In a pioneer for two stories (1.1.02), passes unlock 13 hours after the Chronicles chapter concludes [B02-0005]. **May be out of date:** the same unverified 1.1.12 summary says key Chronicles chapters now unlock on Friday–Saturday [C04-0002], and notes after 1.1.09 are not available, so check in game whether a calendar now exists (gap L-B02-01).

**Role roster (practice, varies by kingdom):** councils split KvK leadership into diplomacy, war leader, data, territory and events, and fill rally, garrison, open-field and flag roles [B02-0003]; recruitment posts list open slots by troop type and fix event times in **UTC** [B02-0004].

**Checklist before registration closes:** written selection criteria for the roster; roster uploaded and code tested; Watchlist reviewed; fight times published in UTC; requirements published (DKP block).
why_md: Domains lock at the end of registration [B02-0001], and the notes do not say whether the roster can be changed afterwards, so treat registration as the deadline. Being left out of the Lost Kingdom feels arbitrary to players when the criteria are not written down; the game gives the king the tool but not the explanation.
uncertain_notes: B01-0500 (day 85–95 / day 100) is verificado/media but from T3 guides of unknown game version. C04-0002 (1.1.12: Eve of the Crusade opening with the Lost Kingdom; Chronicles chapters fixed to Fri–Sat) is a single commercial T3 source, bruto/baixa, not usable as fact. B01-0502 (KvK durations) is contestado/baixa. B02-0005 is organizado/media; its calendar evidence is from 2023–2025 and may be superseded. B02-0003 and B02-0004 (role teams, UTC times) are organizado/baixa: recruitment ads and guide-style posts. Maximum battle-roster size and who besides the king can edit it are not stated.

title: MGE allocation and disputes: choose a model, publish it, log every exception
body_md:
**Practice, varies by kingdom.** Recruitment posts and player reports describe many kingdoms, especially from KvK1 on, running a **fixed** ("controlled") MGE: a published list of who may take the top ranks per event; some keep early or off-season MGE free-for-all [B05-0002].

| Model | How it works | Card |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed by contribution | Top slots go to top DKP/KvK performers | B05-0002 |
| Fixed by role | Rally/garrison leaders get the commanders they need | B05-0002 |
| DKP auction (minority, evidence from 2025 only) | DKP becomes a currency; ranks are auctioned; balances can expire. The auction bot in the evidence is unmaintained since Jan 2025; not a current tool recommendation | B05-0004 |
| Free-for-all | Early game / off-season; family alliances may differ from the core | B05-0002, B04-0003 |
| "Rotation" | Advertised in recruitment posts, never described | B05-0002 |

**Why the top slots matter:** rank rewards are steeply concentrated at the top (one wiki table gives rank 1 as much as ranks 2–3 combined) [B05-0001]. The table is contested; check the in-game event screen.

**Running the cycle (advice):** collect applications (some kingdoms use Discord bots for multilingual MGE forms, outside the game client [B07-0001]); publish the list and the **point cap** for everyone outside it; watch the leaderboard during the event; contact anyone above their slot.

**Disputes:** players report breakers being penalised by kick, forced migration, zeroing or a fine [B05-0003]. Whatever penalty you choose, **write it in the MGE policy before the event** and record each case (who, event, rank taken, decision). No official MGE allocation or violation tool appears in the cards.
why_md: MGE disputes come back every event, and "fair/transparent MGE" is a common recruiting promise [B05-0002], which shows players judge a kingdom by it. A published model and a log of decisions are what make a fixed MGE look fair rather than like hoarding by the council.
uncertain_notes: All cards are below the firm filter. B05-0002 (fixed MGE) is organizado/media, mostly recruitment ads. B05-0004 (DKP auctions) is organizado/media, minoritario, evidence 2025-01 to 2025-05, card validity date passed, and the Auctioneer Bot it cites is unmaintained since 2025-01-28: described only as past practice. B05-0003 (punishments) and B04-0003 (families) are organizado/baixa. B07-0001 is organizado/media. B05-0001 (stage structure and sculpture table) is contestado/baixa: Fandom and another guide disagree on the stage count.

title: Migration intake: game eligibility first, then your own screening
body_md:
**Game rules (checked by the game; a T3 guide says leadership cannot bypass them)** [B06-0002]:
- **Age limits since 1.1.06 (2026-03-24):** same-season into a first-story SoC kingdom: character at most 150 days older than the target kingdom (was 240); cross-season into Season 2: 80 (was 120); into Season 3: 120 (was 180) [B06-0003, C04-0008].
- **New kingdoms** are restricted from same-season immigration until the end of Season 1 (pioneer on select continents) [B06-0003].
- **Cross-season (1.0.83):** refundable 20,000-gem deposit, governors under 10M power ineligible, power limit 85M [C04-0025].
- **Personal requirements (T3):** CH16+, no alliance, a cooldown after migrating, Passport Pages scaled by power [B06-0001].
- **King's levers (T3 guide; not described in official notes):** the normal immigration power cap and approval of **special immigration** above it. Officially, special immigration exists and its records reset after a Kingdom Merger (1.1.03) [B06-0002]. Rules after 1.1.09 are not verified (gap L-B06-03).

**Your screening (practice, varies by kingdom):** application forms and account reviews with minimums (kills, deaths, power, CH25/T5, commanders/equipment), alliance placement and role recruiting, handled by the king or migration officers [B06-0004]. Thresholds vary widely; there is no standard.

**Official alliance tools that help:** passlist (auto-accept, up to 200), Quick Approval of join requests, member search (1.0.91) [B04-0006].

**Do this:** publish the intake rules with **the patch they were checked against**; route every applicant through one officer; place them in an alliance on arrival.
why_md: Migration rules changed in March 2026 [B06-0003], and players are confused by the age rule and by official mails that were withdrawn. In some kingdoms migrants are expected to ask first, and unannounced arrivals are reported to be treated as spies or farms [B03-0006]; a public intake route avoids that conflict.
uncertain_notes: B06-0001 (CH16, passport table, cooldown) is organizado/media from a T3 guide by an account marketplace. B06-0002 (king's cap control) is organizado/media; the cap UI is T3. B06-0004 (kingdom screening) is organizado/media. B03-0006 is organizado/baixa. C04-0008 and C04-0025 are patch-state cards (official notes, bruto). Rules after 1.1.09 are not verified.

title: Exits and enforcement after KvK: notice, deadline, official levers before force
body_md:
**What kingdoms do (practice, varies by kingdom):** after KvK, some leaderships publish who must leave, with a deadline; one kingdom site targets "very low DKP and high power (top 300 in the kingdom)" [B06-0005]. A reported ladder is kick from alliance, an order to migrate within a deadline, then zeroing; it is used for missed DKP, broken MGE agreements, refused orders or unwanted power [B03-0005]. Some kingdoms also tier players into reward / probation / removal [B08-0006].

**Official levers and their limits:**
- **Watchlist** blocks Lost Kingdom entry, but not for the top 50 by power (top 100 in Imperium kingdoms) unless under 50M [B02-0002].
- **Banish** (king, and since 1.0.96 Queen/General/PM) teleports a city to the upper-left province [B03-0003].
- **Alliance blocklist** (up to 200) works per alliance; no kingdom-wide blocklist was found in the notes [B04-0006].
- **SoC home-kingdom territory protection (1.1.03):** governors can no longer attack cities inside other alliances' territory in the home kingdom [C04-0014], which limits zeroing there.
- **Vacation Permit (SoC, 1.0.87):** takes an accepting governor out of the kingdom's matchmaking score for the season (see the SoC block) [B03-0007].

**Do this:** use the written exit rule; send each governor the reason, the numbers and the deadline by mail; record the decision and any appeal; prefer the official levers above.
why_md: Exit lists that target top-300 power accounts touch the same top-300 window used for the kingdom power that drives SoC seeding [B08-0008], so exits change that number. The game gives no notice or appeal tooling, so an exit list without written reasons can look personal. A dated, numeric notice is the only record either side has.
uncertain_notes: B06-0005 (exit lists) and B03-0005 (enforcement ladder) are organizado/media; the two kingdom rule sites behind them share a template, so 'top 300' is one source. B08-0006 (tiering) is organizado/baixa. C04-0014 is a patch-state card (official notes, bruto).

title: Title management: use the official reservation system
body_md:
**Official since 1.0.91:** governors reserve "defender-class" kingdom titles (which titles that covers is not defined, gap L-B03-01) for a time slot; if the king or a ruler (undefined, gap L-B03-04) approves, the title is granted automatically in that slot. Kings/rulers choose which titles are open, can enable **auto-approval** and set reservation durations. Since 1.0.94 each title can require a **City Hall level** and have its own reservation duration, and holders can give a title up [B03-0002].

**Since 1.0.91 each Lost Kingdom domain has its own set of titles**, effective only in the Lost Kingdom (official note quoted on B03-0001).

**Title buffs (two T3 guides, same numbers; verify in game)** [B03-0001]:

| Title | Buff |
|---|---|
| King | +5% troop attack, defense, health |
| Queen | +15% gathering speed |
| General | +5% troop attack, defense |
| Prime Minister | +15% resource production, +10% building speed |
| Justice | +5% attack, +10% march speed |
| Duke | +5% defense, +10% training speed |
| Architect | +10% building speed |
| Scientist | +5% research speed, +10% gold gathering |

Negative titles (Traitor, Beggar, Exile, Slave, Sluggard, Fool) carry penalties [B03-0001]. The same T3 guides say a development title must be active **when the queue starts**.

**Do this:** open the reservable titles, turn on auto-approval with a sensible duration, set the CH requirement, and write in the rules what the leadership titles are used for. Retire manual title queues and title bots where the reservation system covers the title.
why_md: Title queues used to need a person or a paid bot online all day; the reservation system does this in the game [B03-0002]. Which titles count as reservable ("defender-class") is not defined in the notes, so leadership titles may still need a manual rule.
uncertain_notes: B03-0001 (title list and buff values) is organizado/media: two T3 guides that may copy each other, one an account marketplace. The reservation mechanics (B03-0002) are official.

title: Alliance housekeeping with the official tools (and what they don't do)
body_md:
**Permissions (1.0.96):** officer permissions are split into 6 categories (Info, Member, Internal, Building, Garrison/Rally, Admin Management); the leader and Counselors customise each officer title. Since 1.1.03 building dismantling runs on a countdown with a notification, and the leader or a Counselor can cancel it [B04-0001]. **Keep Building and Admin rights with people you trust.**

**Membership:** blocklist (200 since 1.0.96) and passlist (200 since 1.0.91); Quick Approval for join requests; member search; a reason can be given when removing a member [B04-0006, B04-0001].

**Alliance Notes (1.1.07):** notes on members are **visible to all alliance members** — never put warnings, probation or private judgements there [B04-0002].

**Quick Checks (1.1.07):** all online members get a confirm/decline prompt; unlocks when the kingdom enters Season 1 [B04-0002].

**Army Groups and markers (pioneer 1.1.01; Army Groups for all SoC alliances 1.1.02):** governors assign troops to the group, and the creator controls them against enemy field troops and rallies; officers place command and teleport markers on the map [B04-0005]. Whether this works while those members are offline is not stated in the notes.

**Beyond the tools (practice, varies by kingdom):** councils track helps, donations, fort rallies, chat activity and power growth in a sheet or bot to place members and decide kicks [B08-0005]; top alliances run academy and farm alliances as a family [B04-0003]. If you use activity metrics, publish them; members complain about being marked inactive without knowing the measure.
why_md: An officer with the wrong rights can dismantle alliance buildings or edit the alliance; the 1.0.96 categories and the 1.1.03 dismantle countdown reduce that risk only if the leader actually configures them [B04-0001]. Notes being public is easy to miss and turns a private record into a public accusation [B04-0002].
uncertain_notes: B08-0005 (activity metrics) and B04-0003 (alliance families) are organizado/baixa. The contents of each permission category and Army Group size limits are not documented.

title: Season of Conquest: seeding, Vacation Permits, team-ups and votes
body_md:
**Registration** for a SoC story needs City Hall 25 [C04-0033].

**The kingdom power that drives seeding is official math (1.0.95):** each governor's power counts 100% up to 150M, 80% for 150–300M, 50% for 300–500M and 0% above 500M; only the top 300 governors by individual power count (Q&A); the Imperium threshold is 23.5B [B08-0008, C04-0020].

**Vacation Permit (since 1.0.87):** once the kingdom is in SoC the king can issue permits; an accepted permit takes the governor out of the kingdom's **matchmaking score** for the rest of the season; the holder can enter the Lost Kingdom but cannot leave the starting province. Permits can be revoked (1.0.89); the monthly number depends on kingdom activity (1.0.90) [B03-0007]. **Uncertain:** the notes do not say whether this "matchmaking score" is the tiered top-300 kingdom power above (gap L-B03-03). If it is, permits for inactive or farm accounts are a non-violent alternative to zeroing your own players; check before relying on it.

**Votes and diplomacy (official):**
- **Team-up / merger teams (1.1.03):** a team needs at least 2 kingdoms (was 3) and 150 active governors (was 200); team power = sum of top-300 governors, capped at the top-24 kingdoms [B09-0002, C04-0013]. The two cards disagree on whether these rules belong to SoC team-ups or Kingdom Merger teams; the official sentence only says "form a team".
- **Match vote (1.1.03):** a camp refuses its match if more than 80% of the votes within the camp reject the result [B09-0002].
- **Coalitions** start with 4 alliances (1.1.03) [B09-0002].
- **Rest Mode vote** (pioneer, 1.1.08; may not be live in your kingdom): enabled if more than 50% of kingdoms in the Lost Kingdom vote for it; the king's vote covers all domains [B09-0002, C04-0031].
- **Reward sharing (official, 1.1.03):** at A+ the leader of the coalition that captures the Crusader Fortress distributes Autarch Testimonies to camps that did not capture the Great Ziggurat; at S+ the Ziggurat coalition can share a Star of Champions [B09-0003].
- **Camp Treaty:** reported for 1.1.12 as a pioneer by one commercial third-party source only; content unknown [B09-0003].

**Do this:** before each vote, agree in the council how the king votes and write it down; record cross-kingdom agreements (screenshots, dates), since they are not stored in the game.
why_md: The kingdom power that drives seeding is a published formula over the top 300 governors [B08-0008], so a council can see in advance how exits and arrivals move it. The Vacation Permit is a documented, non-violent lever on the matchmaking score [B03-0007], although its link to seeding power is unconfirmed. Votes bind the whole kingdom or camp, so the council should decide them, not the king alone.
uncertain_notes: B09-0003 is organizado/baixa: the Camp Treaty comes from a commercial T3 summary only; the reward-sharing rules in it are official (1.1.03). C04-0013, C04-0020, C04-0031 and C04-0033 are patch-state cards. C04-0013 frames the 2-kingdom/150-governor rule as Kingdom Merger, B09-0002 as SoC team-up. Whether the Vacation Permit's "matchmaking score" equals the tiered top-300 kingdom power is not stated, and the permit allowance per activity level is unknown.

title: Single points of failure: the king, the data officer, the bot author
body_md:
**Mistake: one person holds the kingdom's tools.** Three roles typically do.

| Who | What breaks if they leave | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **King** | King skills, title approvals, roster, Watchlist, votes | Queen/General/PM share Imprison, Exile, Banish, Leader, Inspire since 1.0.96 [B03-0003]; the notes also let "rulers" manage the Watchlist (1.1.03) and approve titles (1.0.91) [B02-0002, B03-0002], but who rulers are is undefined (L-B03-04), so check in game before relying on it; turn on title auto-approval [B03-0002] |
| **Alliance leader** | Permissions, kicks, dismantle cancels | Appoint more than one Counselor: leader and Counselors customise officer permissions and can cancel a dismantle [B04-0001]. Players report ghost alliances with absent leaders and informal hand-downs [B04-0004] |
| **Data officer** | Scans, DKP sheet, requirement lists | Kingdoms are reported to rely on scanners or paid services, then compute DKP in spreadsheets [B08-0003] (ToS risk: see the data block); keep the formula and sheet in a shared council folder and document the steps |
| **Bot author** | Verification, reminders, MGE forms, title queues | Prefer official features where they exist (titles, Quick Checks, Bugle); keep bot settings and ownership shared [B07-0001] |

**Also write down** who replaces whom, and how kingship is passed on. The rules for kingship transfer and for transferring an inactive R5's alliance were not found in patch notes.

**Small official incentive:** Alliance Leadership achievements reward time spent leading (by Jan 2026) [B04-0007].
why_md: Kingdom administration relies on a few volunteers; when one quits, the DKP history, the bot and the king skills can disappear together. Since 1.0.96 five king skills can be shared with Queen, General and Prime Minister [B03-0003], so concentrating them in one person is now avoidable; the other king powers still depend on the king or on the undefined "rulers" [B02-0002].
uncertain_notes: B04-0004 (ghost alliances, informal succession) is organizado/baixa. B08-0003 (time cost from one tool README) and B07-0001 (Discord bots) are organizado/media. Who counts as a "ruler" in 1.1.03 is not defined.

title: Conduct and anti-bot rules: don't run or require scripts, never collect logins
body_md:
**Official:** since 1.1.07 (2026-05-07) players using third-party tools such as scripts or cheats lose **Conduct Score**, and penalties apply below thresholds; it was rolled out first in SoC kingdoms [C04-0006].

**Terms of Service (text shown 2025-04-15):** no engines, robots or data-mining tools to access or download game content other than Lilith-provided software or standard browsers [C02-0003]; no automated access, and **no soliciting other members' login credentials** [C02-0004].

**What this means for a council:**
- **Never require** members to run farming or gathering scripts, and do not tolerate them in your rules.
- **Never ask for logins** to scan, fill events or "pilot" accounts.
- **Scanners** that drive the client through an emulator with ADB [B08-0004] are automation; this guide does not recommend them (see the data block).
- **Discord bots** that only read screenshots or forms run outside the game client [B07-0001]. Whether Conduct Score or the ToS treat them differently from in-game scripts is **not stated** anywhere; data taken from screenshots is still game content.
- Put a conduct line in the written rules.
why_md: A council rule that pushes members toward scripts puts their accounts at risk under an enforced, in-game system [C04-0006]. Asking for logins breaks the ToS outright [C02-0004] and is also how account thefts start.
uncertain_notes: C04-0006 is a patch-state card (official notes, bruto); thresholds and penalties are not published. C02-0003 and C02-0004 are organizado/alta (ToS text). B07-0001 is organizado/media. Whether screenshot-reading Discord bots are outside Conduct Score is this guide's reading of "third-party tools such as scripts or cheats", not an official statement.

body_md:
These would change the advice above. Each is pending in-game measurement (T0) or leader interviews.

| Question | Why it matters | Card |

why_md: Kingdom administration is the area where the official game changed most since 2025, and several of those changes (Toolkit, pioneer features) are not documented anywhere public. Listing them keeps the guide honest about what is not yet known.
uncertain_notes: B02-0005 and B05-0002 are organizado/media; B09-0003 is organizado/baixa (T3 only); C04-0002 is bruto/baixa (one commercial source). The other cards in the table are official notes but leave the listed question open.
